name: The Agency (agency-agents)
works_with: Claude Code natively, plus install scripts for GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, OpenClaw, Qwen Code, Kimi Code, Codex, Osaurus, Hermes and DeepSeek Harness
short: Over 230 ready-made specialist agent personas (frontend dev, security, marketing, sales and more) to install into your coding agent.
what: A collection of more than 230 agent files grouped into divisions such as Engineering, Design, Marketing, Sales, Testing, Security and Game Development. Each file gives an agent a role, workflow, deliverables and success metrics. Scripts convert and install them into the format each coding agent expects.
who: Anyone using an AI coding agent who wants role-specific helpers, for code review, design, marketing copy or project planning. Install only the divisions you need. Skip it if you prefer to write your own short prompts, since the full set is large.
needs: A local copy of the repo to run the scripts (the README does not give a clone command)
Bash to run scripts/convert.sh and scripts/install.sh
Optional: the Agency Agents desktop app for macOS, Linux or Windows instead of the scripts

steps.title: Get the repo
steps.text: Clone or download github.com/msitarzewski/agency-agents and open a terminal in that folder.

steps.title: Generate the files for other tools
steps.text: Claude Code and GitHub Copilot use the agent files as they are. Other tools need this step first.

steps.title: Run the interactive installer
steps.text: It detects which tools you have and lets you tick the ones to install into.

steps.title: Or install only some divisions
steps.text: See the teams and agent counts with --list teams, and add --dry-run to preview.

steps.title: Or use the desktop app on a Mac
steps.text: The app browses the roster, installs agents with a click and keeps them updated.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Use the Frontend Developer agent to review this component.

watch: The installer writes into your tools' config folders, for example ~/.claude/agents/, ~/.codex/agents/ and ~/.gemini/. Cursor, Windsurf, Aider and OpenCode installs write into your current project (.cursor/rules/, .windsurfrules, CONVENTIONS.md, .opencode/agents/).
Read scripts/install.sh before running it, and use --dry-run to see what it will copy.
The README says OpenCode registers only about 119 agents and silently drops the rest. Install a subset with --division to stay under that limit.
For Aider the README says all agent bodies together are about a million tokens, so it installs an index instead of the full text.
